DropUnit.v:11 — lab2_proc_DropUnit — The only streaming val/rdy "drop one packet" filter: a 2-state (pass/drop) FSM that kills the message arriving while `drop` is high (combinationally if already present), parameterized by message width; used by both processor tops to discard late imem responses on squash. Nothing else in either tree drops stream packets.

ProcAlt.v:16 — lab2_proc_ProcAlt — Top level of the FULLY BYPASSED 5-stage pipeline variant; unlike ProcBase it leaves the ctrl/dpath instantiation as the student "LAB TASK" and drives dmem request type_/data from internal signals (store-capable), whereas ProcBase hardcodes dmem requests to READ. Only module representing the to-be-completed bypassed processor.

3. ProcBase.v:17 — lab2_proc_ProcBase — The only COMPLETE, functional processor top level: composes ProcBaseCtrl + ProcBaseDpath + DropUnit with bypass queues (imem depth 2, dmem depth 1, proc2mngr depth 1) and per-stage F/D/X/M/W line tracing; nothing else is a finished pipeline with memory + mngr ports.

4. ProcBaseCtrl.v:12 — lab2_proc_ProcBaseCtrl — The only pipeline control unit: per-stage val/stall/squash (ostall from imem resp, mngr2proc, dmem rdy/resp, proc2mngr rdy; osquash from jumps in D and taken branches in X), TinyRV2 decode via casez opcode patterns, emits pc_sel/reg_en/alu_fn/rf_wen/stats_en_wen plus imem_respstream_drop. Multiplier FSMs have no hazard/branch logic.

5. ProcBaseDpath.v:18 — lab2_proc_ProcBaseDpath — The only full datapath: F–W pipeline register chain, PC + pc+4 + branch/jal target muxes, vc_Regfile_2r1w_zero register file, csrr select mux (mngr2proc/num_cores/core_id), M-stage writeback mux (ALU vs mem), stats_en register; no other module contains a register file or PC logic.

6. ProcDpathAlu.v:10 — lab2_proc_ProcDpathAlu — The only fn-decoded combinational ALU (4'd0 ADD, 4'd11 CP-OP0, 4'd12 CP-OP1; more fns = lab task) with equality and signed/unsigned less-than flag outputs; the multipliers' adders are hardwired shift-add engines, not op-decodable.

7. ProcDpathImmGen.v:9 — lab2_proc_ProcDpathImmGen — The only datapath immediate generator: imm_type-selected 32-bit sign-extended immediate (I- and B-type implemented; S/U/J = lab task). Distinct from InstUnpack (raw field split, no sign-extension/reassembly) and InstTasks (trace-width decode functions, not a ported synthesizable module).

8. tinyrv2_encoding.v:132 — lab2_proc_tinyrv2_encoding_InstTasks — Parameterless container of the only instruction DISASSEMBLY functions: trace-width immediate extractors (imm_i/imm_shamt/imm_s/imm_b/imm_u_sh12/imm_j), 25-char disasm, and 4-char disasm_tiny for all TinyRV2 opcodes; no ports; nothing else formats instructions as strings.

9. tinyrv2_encoding.v:345 — lab2_proc_tinyrv2_encoding_InstUnpack — The only purely combinational 32-bit-instruction field splitter emitting opcode/rd/rs1/rs2/funct3/funct7/csr; instantiated in both ProcBaseCtrl and ProcBaseDpath, but no other module produces this full 7-field unpack.

10. tinyrv2_encoding.v:377 — lab2_proc_tinyrv2_encoding_InstTrace — The only module whose sole behavior is appending instruction disasm (disasm | disasm_tiny) to the vc_trace line-trace string (`ifndef SYNTHESIS guarded, no functional outputs); other trace users do it inline.

=== lab1_imul (2 .v files, 7 modules) ===

11. IntMulAlt.v:12 — lab1_imul_IntMulTrailingZero — The only priority encoder in either tree: scans a 32-bit input for its least-significant set bit and outputs its index (5-bit trailing-zero count).

12. IntMulAlt.v:34 — lab1_imul_IntMulAltDpath — VARIABLE-LATENCY shift-add datapath: unlike IntMulBaseDpath's one-bit-per-cycle shift, it skips runs of zeros per iteration (adds a << trailing_zeros into the result, shifts A past the set bit, shifts B by tz+1) and exports b_is_zero plus a 6-bit shift_amount status instead of b_lsb.

13. IntMulAlt.v:163 — lab1_imul_IntMulAltCtrl — Variable-latency controller: same IDLE/CALC/DONE skeleton as IntMulBaseCtrl but exits CALC early on b_is_zero and advances the counter by shift_amount (not +1/cycle); has no add_mux_sel output. Only controller whose iteration count depends on operand data.

14. IntMulAlt.v:278 — lab1_imul_IntMulAlt — Top level of the VARIABLE-LATENCY multiplier (early termination when multiplier bits exhausted) wiring AltCtrl+AltDpath, with line tracing that includes per-iteration shift amount; distinct from IntMulBase (fixed 32-cycle latency) and from processor tops (standalone val/rdy streaming unit, no memory ports).

15. IntMulBase.v:15 — lab1_imul_IntMulBaseDpath — FIXED-LATENCY shift-add datapath: A shifts left 1 and B shifts right 1 every cycle, b_lsb gating the add mux (accumulate A or pass result through); exports b_lsb status and a/b/result internals for tracing — one bit per iteration, no zero skipping.

16. IntMulBase.v:135 — lab1_imul_IntMulBaseCtrl — Fixed-latency controller: runs CALC for exactly 32 cycles (counter == 6'd32), drives a/b/result mux selects and asserts add_mux_sel = b_lsb; the only controller with a hardwired constant iteration count regardless of operand values.

17. IntMulBase.v:250 — lab1_imul_IntMulBase — Top level of the FIXED-LATENCY 32×32→32 unsigned multiplier: takes {a,b} packed in a 64-bit istream message, product on 32-bit ostream after a constant 32 CALC cycles, IDLE/CALC/DONE val/rdy handshake and state/counter line tracing.
